source_profile: Current workspace robot visual GLBs; no geometry, normals, grouping or source assets edited by this review.
method: Downloaded manufacturer photos/PDFs, rendered PDF first pages using pdftoppm and actually viewed local image pixels. Compared component boundaries with current named GLB material partitions. Color candidates are visual approximations; photos are not calibrated color/BRDF measurements.

sources.summary: KUKA announced that its next AGILUS generation would replace standard sixx variants from late2017, use white as standard like KR3, and allow other colors by request.

models.variant_note: Exact model designation matched in official datasheet. Standard industrial-yellow version reviewed; food-grade, clean-room or customer special paint is outside this conclusion.

parts.observation: The manufacturer M-10iD/12 photo shows a black robot base casting, including the integrated rear enclosure. This is the robot footprint, not a separately added installation pedestal.
Yellow J1/body shell; its source yellow material is distinct from black motor and service covers.
Yellow forearm with black end/service housing; retain both groups.
Visible wrist and front interface appear black in the official standard industrial-yellow model photo.
Black front interface in same-model official image; no basis to make it bright silver.
Black motor/service covers and black dress components in official photo. Other links also retain their existing black groups.

models.variant_note: URDF/file named M_20iA; attached 2019 sheet identifies 35M but kinematics are shared with 20M. Exact payload/production revision remains unverified.

parts.observation: Official M-20iA/20M and /35M photos clearly separates a dark charcoal conical robot base casting from the jet-black J1 ring above it. Current BaseLink is near jet black; a restrained charcoal candidate can recover this distinction.
Official 20M/35M photos and the local 35M documentation share the yellow industrial body. Current model is named only M_20iA, so payload variant is not established by its filename.

Distal wrist assembly is black in official image.

Official 20M/35M front mounting interface appears dark; current .8 linear highly metallic group appears too pale. Photograph cannot establish whether this is black coating or treated metal, so evaluate a dark metal candidate without asserting factory BRDF.

Both official photos show black motor bodies with red end caps and black cable dress parts; the 35M also shows a light gray external cable loop. Existing CAD black partitions are shared across multiple components, so an entire black material must not be recolored red or gray.

base_followup_review.shared_group_limitation: Base casting, rear connector housing and small fittings are merged. KR10_R1100_2 also has rear cable/line geometry in the same gray group.
base_followup_review.verdict: Retain source base color and finish for now. A high-metallic trial darkens in the area-light-only EEVEE studio; do not compensate for missing image-based reflections by raising baseColor. OEM photographs show a metallic-gray appearance but cannot distinguish bare metal from metallic paint or identify a calibrated BRDF.

flange_followup_review.verdict: Dark gray interface follows the predominantly black treated-metal tool flange visible in the official2017 product photos more closely than the prior pale-gray whole group. Keep source metallic/roughness; small exposed silver regions/holes remain a single-group approximation.

conclusions: No evidence that any of these four standard FANUC robot base castings should be recolored yellow.
M-10iD/12 near-black base matches exact-model official photo.
M-20iA near-black casting loses a charcoal-versus-black-ring distinction; trial a modest charcoal base. Variant uncertainty remains explicit.
M-710iC/70 and R-2000iC/165F .4 linear gray castings are too pale compared with same-model official photos; trial a dark charcoal finish.
FANUC official body photos appear brighter/canary-yellow than current #F4CB16 studio render; test a restrained candidate with unchanged lighting rather than claim a factory paint code.
Red motor caps and gray cable components cannot be safely recovered by repainting merged black material groups. Keep them until geometry-specific assignment is established.
limitations: Manufacturer photos have exposure, white balance, specular reflection and compression differences; no exact certified paint/RAL claim is made.
The official FANUC datasheet download endpoint redirects to the manufacturer Craft CDN; both original and effective URLs/hashes are recorded.
Some older FANUC EU/Japan PDF URLs returned410/404; they are not treated as newly viewed photo evidence.
No dealer imagery used as primary evidence.
A candidate whole GLB must never overwrite a later normal refinement: apply only reviewed material JSON on the latest source after checking its nonmaterial state.

key_decisions: FANUC castings dark by model; M10 black retained; three component corrections reviewed and adopted by parent.
Hans E05/E10 Link6 silver mounting interface is better represented as brushed metal than white plastic.
ROKAE white/pale-blue/metal partition is sensible; pale-blue trial remains optional.
KUKA standard AGILUS-2/KR3 moving body white is explicitly supported by OEM; orange is an available requested alternative; old sixx orange retained.
Preserve dark motor/service covers as painted or polymer surfaces unless component-specific evidence supports bare metal.
